transcript: Last night, I was at the first preview of Give Me Carmelita Tropicana! at Soho Rep by Alina Troyano and Branden Jacobs-Jenkins. Starring Alina as her persona / alter ego Carmelita Tropicana, a downtown performance artist who was particularly prominent in the 80s and 90s, this play is a very meta and fantastical account of Alina considering the retirement of Carmelita, and Branden attempting to buy her instead. From there, Carmelita kinda takes on a life of her own and things get really weird really fast. You'll ask yourself multiple times throughout the piece, what is going on? But somehow it comes together as an interesting exploration of ownership, representation and identity, legacy, and nostalgia. It was cool to see a very non-traditional piece by Branden Jacobs-Jenkins but the text still had the sharpness that I've noticed in his other work. And although parts of the show were a little out there for me to fully understand and contextualize, I think it's intentionally a bit hazy and the broad strokes of the story come through enough that there's plenty to engage with no matter how experimental your taste is. With that, another program for my collection.
